tone_statements.quote: Tone Marks in Nkwen Language: Acute ΄ Grave ̀ Rising ̌ falling ̂ We observe four tone marks but mark only three of them; the Low tone (grave), the high tone (acute), the low-high (falling tone) and the high-low (rising tone). We do not mark the high tone. High a - Sama / a name ... Low à - àkòɂò/a toilet ... Low-high (falling tone) ǎ - bǎtǝ̂ /to split ... High-low (rising tone) â - mǝ̀fâ /twins

sources.locator: slide headed 'Tone Marks in Nkwen Language' (p. 13 is only the section-title slide 'Bǝ̀ndǝ̀-nji Tone marks'; the table continues on p. 15; the bare tone-diacritic grids are on pp. 3-4)
sources.note: Orthographic tone lesson. States four tone marks of which three are written: Low (grave), High (acute, left unmarked), 'low-high' and 'high-low' contours (the deck swaps the labels falling/rising relative to the diacritics: caron = low-high, circumflex = high-low), with example words for each vowel (e.g. a Sama 'a name' H, akoʔo 'toilet' L, batə 'to split' LH, məfa 'twins' HL) and the remark that tone marks on vowels change their sound/meaning. No analysis of downstep or grammatical tone.
